facts.statement: Tataouinea was an extinct sauropod dinosaur that lived in Tunisia during the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Tataouinea is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur in the subfamily Rebbachisaurinae of Rebbachisauridae which lived in the Early Cretaceous of Tunisia.

facts.statement: Tataouinea lived in what is now Africa during the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 112 to 109 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, entre 112 a 109 millones de años, durante el Albiense, en lo que ahora es África.

facts.statement: The first elements of the holotype specimen were discovered in 2011 by Aldo Luigi Bacchetta, though excavation did not begin until 2012.
facts.quote: The first known elements of the holotype were discovered in the Aïn el Guettar Formation in 2011 by Aldo Luigi Bacchetta, but he was unable to excavate the specimen until 2012.

facts.statement: The fossil remains were studied by Federico Fanti, Andrea Cau, Mohsen Hassine, and Michela Contessi.
facts.quote: The remains were subsequently studied by Federico Fanti, Andrea Cau, Mohsen Hassine and Michela Contessi.

facts.statement: The genus Tataouinea was officially named in 2013.
facts.quote: The genus was named in 2013.

facts.statement: In 2015, additional material including tail vertebrae was uncovered and analyzed after the initial description.
facts.quote: In 2015 more material of the holotype specimen was uncovered after the initial description were analysed. These included additional tail vertebrae.

facts.statement: The genus name refers to the region of Tataouine where it was found, while the species name honors Hannibal, the Carthaginian military commander.
facts.quote: El género fue nombrado oficialmente en 2013. El nombre del género es en referencia a la región en la cual fue descubierto, Tataouine, mientras que el epíteto de la especie es en honor de Aníbal, el comandante militar cartaginense durante la segunda guerra púnica.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, cataloged as ONM DT 1-36, consisted of pelvic bone fragments, several tail vertebrae, and sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo descubierto por el equipo de Fanti fue catalogado como ONM DT 1-36, constaba de fragmentos de huesos pélvicos, varias vértebras caudales y sacras.

facts.statement: Tataouinea's bones were extensively pneumatic, supporting the theory that sauropods possessed bird-like respiratory systems.
facts.quote: Its bones were extensively pneumatic, providing strong support for the theory that sauropods had birdlike respiratory systems.

facts.statement: Tataouinea was likely a relatively small, four-legged, herbivorous sauropod with a short neck, a long whip-like tail, and a light build.
facts.quote: Al igual que otros miembros de Rebbachisauridae, incluido el Nigersaurus bien estudiado, probablemente era un dinosaurio herbívoro de cuatro patas relativamente pequeño con un cuello corto, una cola larga en forma de látigo y una constitución ligera.

facts.statement: Tataouinea was the second-largest known member of the family Rebbachisauridae, after Limaysaurus tessonei.
facts.quote: El tamaño exacto de Tataouinea es desconocido, pero era el animal más grande de la familia Rebbachisauridae después de Limaysaurus tessonei.

facts.statement: The skull of Tataouinea was likely pneumatized through multiple holes, similar to Nigersaurus.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Tataouinea, como el de Nigersaurus, probablemente fue neumatizado a través de múltiples agujeros.

facts.statement: Tataouinea had a notably wide snout with teeth only on the front of the jaw, resembling a vacuum cleaner.
facts.quote: El hocico era notablemente más ancho que la parte posterior de la cabeza, la mandíbula del dinosaurio, que tenía dientes solo en la parte delantera, se asemejaba a una aspiradora.

facts.statement: Until Tataouinea was discovered, similar structures had not been found in the ischial bones of other dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Hasta el momento del descubrimiento de Tataouinea, no se había encontrado estructuras similares en los huesos isquiáticos de otros dinosaurios.

facts.statement: The spinous processes of the sacral vertebrae fused to create a soft-tissue hump or sail, similar to Dicreosaurus.
facts.quote: Las apófisis espinosas de las vértebras sacras se soldaron y crearon una "vela" o joroba de tejidos blandos, como en Dicreosaurus.

facts.statement: The large neural processes of the vertebrae were shaped like an inverted Y.
facts.quote: Los grandes procesos neuronales tenían la forma de una Y invertida.

facts.statement: Researchers believe Tataouinea had a respiratory system similar to modern birds due to its unusually pneumatized bones.
facts.quote: Los huesos inusualmente neumatizados de Tataouinea llevaron a los investigadores a pensar que el animal tiene un sistema respiratorio similar al de las aves modernas.

facts.statement: The presence of large pneumatic openings in the pelvic bones suggests a plausible internal ventilation system within the pelvic girdle.
facts.quote: Dado que, en la muestra ONM DT 1-36, también están presentes grandes aberturas neumáticas en los huesos pélvicos, que están lejos del contacto directo con el esqueleto axial, la suposición de la presencia de un "sistema de ventilación" en el interior de la cintura pélvica , incluso con el enfoque más conservador, parece plausible.

facts.statement: Vertebral morphology indicates Tataouinea was a rebbachisaurid closely related to European nigersaurines.
facts.quote: Key characteristics of its vertebral morphology show that Tatouinea was a rebbachisaurid, closely related to the nigersaurines of Europe.

facts.statement: A phylogenetic analysis found a clade including Rebbachisaurus, leading to the renaming of the subfamily to Rebbachisaurinae.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis was published alongside the paper, finding a clade of nigersaurines to include Rebbachisaurus, thus forcing the subfamily to be renamed Rebbachisaurinae.

facts.statement: Tataouinea fossils were found in the Jebel El Mra or Oum ed Diab members of the Aptian-Albian Aïn el Guettar Formation.
facts.quote: Tataouinea was discovered in the Jebel El Mra Member or the nearby Oum ed Diab Member of the Aptian-Albian Aïn el Guettar Formation.

facts.statement: It is noted that the pneumatization of Rebbachisauridae skeletons developed gradually, becoming more pronounced in the Rebbachisaurinae subfamily.
facts.quote: La neumatización de los esqueletos de los miembros de la familia Rebbachisauridae se desarrolló gradualmente, lo que es más notorio al examinar los huesos de animales de la subfamilia Rebbachisaurinae.

facts.statement: In its 2013 description, Fanti and colleagues placed Tataouinea in the subfamily Nigersaurinae of the family Rebbachisauridae.
facts.quote: En la primera descripción de 2013, Fanti y sus colegas ubicaron a Tataouinea en la subfamilia Nigersaurinae de la familia Rebbachisauridae

facts.statement: Together with its sister group Limaysaurinae, Nigersaurinae forms the clade Khebbashia.
facts.quote: Junto con su grupo hermano, Limaysaurinae, Nigersaurinae forma el clado Khebbashia

facts.statement: A 2015 description noted an evolutionary relationship between Nigersaurus, Demandasaurus, and Tataouinea.
facts.quote: Una descripción de 2015 señaló una relación evolutiva entre Nigersaurus, Demandasaurus y Tataouinea

facts.statement: Tataouinea was quadrupedal because its front legs were shorter, causing its hips to rise above its hips.
facts.quote: Tataouinea era cuadrúpedo, debido al hecho de que las patas delanteras eran más cortas, las caderas del dinosaurio se elevaban por encima de la cruz

facts.statement: Its extremely long tail was likely used as a weapon, similar to other Diplodocus-related dinosaurs.
facts.quote: La cola era extremadamente larga, probablemente, como otros dinosaurios relacionados con Diplodocus, fue utilizado como arma

facts.statement: Paleontologists often find multiple sauropod fossils in small areas, suggesting herd behavior, though only one Tataouinea individual is known.
facts.quote: A menudo, al estudiar fósiles de saurópodos, los paleontólogos encuentran restos fósiles de varios individuos en un área bastante pequeña, lo que indica indirectamente la naturaleza de manada de estos dinosaurios

facts.statement: Known Tataouinea fossils were found in the Ain el-Gutter Formation near Oum ed-Diab, dating to the Early Albian.
facts.quote: Se han encontrado restos conocidos de Tataouinea en las areniscas de la Formación Ain el-Gutter, en la parte de Oum ed-Diab, que datan de la Edad Albiana Temprana

facts.statement: The Oum ed-Diab area consisted of shallow, intertidal, and non-marine deposits on a low coastal plain with sparse vegetation, bordering the newly formed Atlantic Ocean.
facts.quote: Oum ed-Diab alterna entre depósitos poco profundos, intermareales y no marinos formados en una tierra baja costera con escasa vegetación y una costa arenosa bañada por las olas del Océano Atlántico recién formado

facts.statement: As herbivores, Tataouinea fed on common gymnosperms of the time, including conifers.
facts.quote: Siendo dinosaurios herbívoros, Tataouinea se alimentaba de las gimnospermas más comunes de la época, incluidas las coníferas

facts.statement: Tataouinea likely ate low plants to avoid competition with large titanosaurs adapted to high-growing foliage.
facts.quote: Es probable que los dinosaurios Tataouinea comieran plantas bajas para evitar la competencia con los grandes titanosaurianos, que están mejor adaptados para comer hojas y agujas de crecimiento alto

facts.statement: Tataouinea's tooth shape indicated it simply plucked vegetation without chewing it.
facts.quote: La forma de los dientes de Tataouinea indicaba que los animales simplemente arrancaban la vegetación sin masticarla

facts.statement: Like other sauropods, Tataouinea likely swallowed small stones called gastrolites to grind unchewed plant material for digestion.
facts.quote: Como todos los saurópodos, Tataouinea probablemente tragó pequeños guijarros, llamados gastrolitos, de modo que, moliéndolos en una pulpa de material vegetal sin masticar dentro del estómago, ayudó a la digestión de los alimentos

facts.statement: Evidence shows Rebbachisauridae members existed simultaneously on both sides of the Tethys Ocean.
facts.quote: Demostrando que los miembros de la familia Rebbachisauridae existieron simultáneamente en ambos lados del Océano Tetis

facts.statement: The Tethys Ocean flooding parts of North Africa forced dinosaurs to migrate south.
facts.quote: Cuando el Océano Tetis que inundó parte del norte de África obligó a los dinosaurios a migrar hacia el sur

facts.statement: Nigersaurus taqueti was more than one-third smaller than Tataouinea hannibalis.
facts.quote: Nigersaurus taqueti, fue más de un tercio más pequeño que Tataouinea hannibalis

facts.statement: The genus Tataouinea was named by Fanti et al. in 2013.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Tataouinea (genus), Fanti et al. 2013

facts.statement: Tataouinea lived from 113.2 to 100.5 million years ago during the Albian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Tataouinea is Rebbachisaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Rebbachisaurinae

facts.statement: Tataouinea belongs to the family Rebbachisauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Rebbachisauridae

facts.statement: Tataouinea is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Tataouinea has been recorded.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1
